summary: Port Hardy Airport serves as the main aviation gateway to the northern tip of Vancouver Island in British Columbia, Canada. It provides essential connectivity for the remote community of Port Hardy and supports access to nearby outdoor destinations including Cape Scott Provincial Park and the Broughton Archipelago. The airport plays a key role in regional air travel, hosting scheduled services to Vancouver and serving as a hub for charter and float plane operations.
faqs:
Q: What airlines operate from Port Hardy Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by Pacific Coastal Airlines, which offers scheduled flights to Vancouver and other regional destinations. Charter and float plane operators also use the facility.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Port Hardy?
A: Port Hardy Airport is located approximately 10 km southwest of the town center, with a typical drive time of around 15 minutes.

Q: Does Port Hardy Airport have customs and immigration services?
A: Yes, the airport is a designated port of entry with Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) clearance available for international and transborder flights.

Q: Are there car rental services at the airport?
A: Yes, car rental counters are available in the terminal building for visitors needing ground transportation.
transport_tips: Rental cars are available at the terminal and are the most convenient option for exploring the North Island, though booking in advance is recommended during summer months. Taxi services operate from the airport but may be limited, so calling ahead is advisable. The scenic drive into Port Hardy along Highway 19 passes through forests and offers glimpses of the coastline.
local_tip: If you're heading out on a wilderness adventure to Cape Scott or the remote north island beaches, book a morning flight to maximize your daylight hours on the trails.
